answer.answer: Audit-ready checkpoint persisted as `.straylight/checkpoints/fde1490b-969c-779f-73f6-cd51bd610fbc.md`. The import remains preserved and auditable without becoming a competing canonical snapshot, and rejected Flowworks work remains historical only.

claims.value: The completed import preserves the original `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` (21,674,717 bytes; SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`) and a verified extracted tree under Git-ignored `raw/`. The ZIP contains 123 entries including directories and 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`; `unzip -t` passed and every packaged SHA-256 passed. Tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` retain full auditability while the duplicate third-party corpus, personalized save context, generated binaries, and legacy SQLite database remain local rather than entering Git.

The archive's repeated numeric-data claim of Steam build `23761620` is corrected: it was only the latest public executable observed, Hotfix `0.2.8`, and is not proven provenance for every source value. The source/game-data axis is Update 1 internal version `35118973`, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441` (inferred `0.2.0`). The source-snapshot axis is canonical immutable snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, using SRDB `2.3.4` retrieved at `2026-07-11 05:02:30 UTC`. The archive itself was retrieved at `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`; its source-site version and reliable claimed game build were not recorded. Its numeric reports remain legacy calculations until actually ported and rerun against the canonical snapshot.

The archive's 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantically deduplicated against the richer RuptureOps corpus and were not installed as a competing snapshot. Selective promotion was limited to `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`; six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v2 impure/pure recipe-producer associations in `sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json`; explicit medium-confidence consumable-effect assumptions with provenance warnings in `sources/consumable-effects.json`; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected an `airlock` item overwritten by a building-shaped detail response and a literal `$undefined` Training Corporation index. The legacy SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, core delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script remain preserved only under `raw/`; no second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is superseded audit history only: its buffer-heavy approach was explicitly rejected and must not become current guidance. The active staged Flowworks plan reaches a level-10 cell with one Stabilizer, one Nozzle, one Impeller, two Valves, one Turbine, and two Pumps; the second Stabilizer is deferred, and HRS v2 is only an evidence-triggered recovery option. Current authority remains the RuptureOps canonical pipeline: `current.json` points to immutable snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, and SQLite is rebuilt from complete canonical snapshots while prior snapshots remain intact. Legacy archive reports retain their July 8 boundary and cannot be relabeled with the canonical snapshot ID until ported and rerun.

claims.value: The older provisional Grand Basin identification with the Red Lake/Redleaf basin was wrong. Grand Basin is the broad basin north of the active production corridor, immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry”; Mythic Cry is in the mountains immediately west. The Grand Basin marker identifies the basin area, not a future Core.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Flowworks is the selected site between Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. It remains a proposed footprint, not a placed Core. Together, Landerworks, Flowworks, and Faraday form the active western/southwestern production corridor; Grand Basin lies north of that corridor.

The overview pins are visually terrain-registered and relational rather than surveyed coordinates: Flowworks is proposed, the Grand Basin marker denotes an area rather than a Core, Faraday is terrain-registered rather than directly labeled in its crop, and the exact Sunstone Station and Brimstone Utility pins remain open. Planning-note coordinates identify SRDB markers. Do not combine the screenshot-registration frame with SRDB map coordinates unless a transform is verified.

The first Goethite satellite is the safer northwestern triple northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin; the first preferred Oil satellite is west/southwest of Grand Basin. The recorded plan uses three Goethite extractors at 45/min with one Goethite-only Cargo Dispatcher/Receiver pair feeding one V2 buffer, and one Oil extractor at 10/min with one Crude-only Cargo pair feeding one V2 buffer and one GB-A Refinery. The rationale is that Goethite and Crude Oil are compact when extracted but expand heavily during processing, so ship each raw resource through its own Cargo link and process beside Grand Basin consumers instead of consuming world-trunk capacity with expanded intermediates. These quantities derive from older July 8 analysis and must be rerun against the canonical RuptureOps snapshot before app publication.

answer.answer: The duplicate archive-import forks are coordinated around the existing verified reconciliation. Replay identity is fixed by the archive hash and import ID; no repository promotion or dirty-worktree mutation was performed. One continuation checkpoint was committed for all forks to resume.

claims.value: The historical topology contains seven related tasks: `019f4f6d-169c-70e2-8de4-81722b41eee9` (initial Update 1 research/bootstrap), `019f5263-8bae-7d10-b944-0fd4a543afb9` (clean RuptureOps bootstrap and repository/vault split), `019f52a5-72aa-7c11-853c-5de258361b42` (general import/reconciliation), `019f52fa-6195-7701-96a2-da6ec7ef7a08` (live exploration continuation), `019f52fa-6917-78a3-b1e5-7e631263b4a5` (logistics fork), `019f52fa-7180-7552-a3b1-09be4c3ee493` (exploration fork carrying the same inherited import request), and `019f531d-ba10-7d50-958e-4cffc089c334` (rupture-cycle product research and interrupted native build). Several forks inherited the exact same `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` request; they are replays, not independent imports or corroboration.

Idempotent identity is the pair of `import_id` `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z` and source-archive SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`. The ledger records `imported_at` `2026-07-11T19:54:52Z`, byte size `21674717`, `115` manifested files, `CHECKSUMS.sha256`, and `integrity_status` `verified`. A matching inherited request must reuse the immutable source copies and existing reconciliation receipts rather than create another import or promotion.

The canonical output is the single successful reconciliation into snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, not the external package as a competing snapshot. The package remains a locally preserved external research import; duplicate item, building, recipe, progression, export, map, loot, and official-news material was not promoted. Only distinct evidence was promoted: six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v2 impure/pure producer links, provenance-warned consumable effects, a player save-state model, and player-specific notes/screenshots. Legacy reports retain their July 8 boundary and must not be relabeled canonical until ported and rerun. Raw imported content remains Git-ignored. Because other native work historically began on dirty `main` and stayed under `ios/`, dirty-tree safety here means leaving active files untouched: no branch, stash, overwrite, repository write, or duplicate promotion was performed.

Exactly one shared continuation checkpoint was committed: `checkpoint:f34c0a2a-7f48-3557-5418-70e7b8aaf8bb` at `.straylight/checkpoints/f34c0a2a-7f48-3557-5418-70e7b8aaf8bb.md`. Future inherited forks should compare the exact archive SHA-256 and import ID, inspect the existing ledger and curated boundary, and resume from this checkpoint without promoting again. The separate iPhone simulator/install-ready acceptance condition remains unverified and must not be inferred complete from historical evidence.

Treat the existing successful reconciliation as canonical.
Keep legacy July 8 calculations at their original provenance boundary until ported and rerun.

For native app continuation, verify current repository truth and explicit acceptance gates without disturbing dirty work.
